solves.reasoning: In academia you come up with a hypothesis (A), not a conclusion first. Online readers lack patience (B), not courage. The vast majority (C) know from the beginning — not minority.

(A) groundbreaking fits the pair 'exciting or groundbreaking'. (B) dwindle fits 'trail off' — readership decreases. (C) journalistic fits 'in journalistic terms' — the text says journalism, not academia.
Online readers don't want to wait for the big reveal (A). You need to tell them up front (B), not in detail which is different. You need to grab (C) their attention, not release it.
③ boring is wrong: the passage says the opening line being particularly interesting makes readers stay — boring contradicts the logic that an interesting hook keeps readers.
② flourish is wrong: readership may still 'flourish and trail off' is contradictory — you cannot flourish and trail off simultaneously. The original is 'dwindle and trail off'.
④ lose is wrong: if you lose their attention early, convincing more readers makes no sense. The original says 'grab' their attention early.
In academic writing, you first come up with a hypothesis before doing experiments. The blank follows 'I came up with a ___', so hypothesis fits perfectly.
The context is getting attention early so you can ___ readers to stay. 'Convince' means persuade to stay — force/allow/prevent don't fit the positive persuasion context.
The blank comes after 'exciting or ___' — a paired positive description. 'Groundbreaking' (innovative) pairs naturally with 'exciting'. Ordinary, controversial, lengthy don't fit as positives.
Dwindle means to gradually decrease. Among choices: decrease(감소하다) is the closest synonym. Multiply, stabilize, intensify all mean different things.
Convince means to persuade. Persuade(설득하다) is the direct synonym. Compel implies force, deceive means trick, distract means to divert attention.
Groundbreaking means innovative/revolutionary. 'Innovative' is the closest synonym among the choices. Conventional is antonym, superficial/repetitive are unrelated.
Majority means the greater part. The antonym is minority. Plurality, entirety, authority are not antonyms.
Dramatic means striking/impressive. Mundane (평범한/일상적인) is the antonym. Theatrical/vivid/emotional are all related to dramatic in meaning, not antonyms.
(A) 'over the course of your writing' = 글쓰기가 진행되는 과정(동안). (B) 'enrolled in an advanced course' = 대학에서 수강하는 강좌. So (A)과정 - (B)강좌.
'The quality of being able to endure waiting or delay without becoming annoyed or upset' = patience (인내심). Courage is for danger, curiosity is desire to know, enthusiasm is eagerness.
drama → dramatic (adjective) to modify the noun 'conclusion'. 'your dramatic conclusion' is the original text.
particular → particularly (adverb) to modify the adjective 'interesting'. 'is particularly interesting' requires an adverb.

The blank precedes 'you can more likely convince more readers to stay'. The passage says grab their attention early = more readers stay. Choice 3 'grab their attention early' directly matches the passage logic.

The blank follows 'Instead,' and precedes '"I proved this!"'. Online readers want the conclusion first — 'you need to tell us up front' matches perfectly. Building suspense or hiding conclusions are the opposite of the point.
